s: Commonly used for Asado-style, open fire cooking, this Argentinian cut is very rarely seen in the states. The vacio (pronounced vah-SEE-oh) is made up of the inner skirt steak, flank steak, and bavette steak. This large cut is made for slow cooking and feeding a crowd, with fat and membranes left on to protect and baste the meat while it cooks, and to crisp up for delicious crunchy fat.
